Concentration-round first-touch: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:cli` (lands in `packages/runtime`'s `AppPlugin`).

Scope in the card's own order — the cheap question gates the expensive work: **step 1 only** as dispatched scope: establish whether a hosted tenant kernel takes the inline-seed branch (one log line or one assertion in an existing multi-tenant harness; the cloud container itself is off-limits per the cloud#1560 ruling the card cites). Branch not taken in production ⇒ report and close as single-tenant `os dev` cost, no further work. Branch taken ⇒ report back with the reading; the ledger-shaped fix (know the seed union is applied rather than re-pay 3 legs/record) is then re-graded with the measured stakes — it is cloud#1561's shape and may want that PR's author-context. Related bare cards #10946/#10945 (same boot-cost family) are still awaiting sweep — the dev should not fold them in uninvited. Size S for step 1.

## The blocking fact, now measured — hosted-tenant kernel posture is **WALLED**, not single

Incoming `domain:cli` seat, session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`. ⛔ Not a grading, ⛔ not a decision — supplying the fact the outgoing seat correctly refused to infer from circumstantial evidence.

### Why this seat could answer it when the last one could not

The outgoing shift recorded this as structurally unanswerable: *「本仓结构性答不了（ArtifactKernelFactory 在 cloud 发行版，@objectstack/organizations 本地没装），本 session 作用域不含 cloud 仓」*. That was true of **that session's authorization surface**, not of the question. I attached `objectstack-ai/cloud` to this session (it was needed anyway to judge #10938's `Blocked-by: cloud#944`), so the reading is now takeable.

⭐ Worth recording as a lane reading: **"this repo cannot answer it" and "this session cannot answer it" are different claims**, and the second one expires the moment scope changes. The predecessor was right not to guess; it just did not need to stay unanswered.

### The reading — cloud @ `b7d3dafe`

Taken from the **live source**, then corroborated by the changeset that put it there (⛔ not the other way round — a changeset describes a change, the source is the current state):

`packages/objectos-runtime/src/artifact-kernel-factory.ts`:

```
// Per-project SecurityPlugin — provides RBAC + tenant_isolation RLS.
// Multi-tenant deployments additionally register OrganizationsPlugin (@objectstack/organizations),
// which provides organization_id auto-stamping, per-org seed …

// … `tenant_isolation` RLS when the scoping plugin is absent —
// so OrganizationsPlugin (@objectstack/organizations) MUST be registered before SecurityPlugin.
```

And `.changeset/drop-dangling-plugin-org-scoping-link.md`, on the same tree:

> ADR-0081 moved multi-org row scoping out of the open framework … the code migrated here as the proprietary `@objectstack/organizations`. The runtime half of that migration is long done — **`ArtifactKernelFactory` imports `@objectstack/organizations` and, per ADR-0093 D5, fails CLOSED when it cannot load it.**

### What that establishes, and what it does not

**Established:** a hosted tenant kernel is **walled**. Row scoping is real (`organization_id` auto-stamping via `OrganizationsPlugin`), it is ordered before `SecurityPlugin` by an explicit ordering requirement, and the kernel **fails closed** rather than degrading to unscoped if the plugin cannot load. So "hosted tenant = single-org, no wall" is ruled out.

⛔ **Not established, and I am not stretching the reading to cover it:** how many organizations a *typical* hosted environment actually carries at boot, which is the number this card's seed-cost arithmetic (3 sequential round trips per seed record) is ultimately sensitive to. The wall existing tells you the seed path is per-org scoped; it does not tell you the multiplier. If the card's cost estimate turns on that count, that is a **second** fact and it is not this one.

Leaving the card in `needs-user-decision` — the fact is supplied, the decision is not mine.

## Maintainer ruling recorded (atomic four-part write)

Ruled 2026-08-23, live PM chat, verbatim: 「10950 不考虑存量，其他接受你的建议」 — this card falls under the accepted recommendations. **Ruled: settle on the reading, then act** — posture is established WALLED (cli seat's source reading), but whether a hosted tenant kernel actually takes the AppPlugin inline-seed branch per boot is still one log line / one assertion away. `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke (`domain:cli`). Dispatch shape: Step 1 take that single reading (coordinate with the repo:cloud seat if a hosted container is needed); if the branch IS taken ⇒ implement the seed-ledger short-circuit (cloud#1561 shape; batching helps genuine first seeds too); if NOT taken ⇒ close as single-tenant `os dev` cost with the reading attached. Premise-first: stopping after Step 1 with a negative reading is a complete, valid delivery.

## Step 1 settled: a hosted tenant kernel does **NOT** take the inline-seed branch

`domain:cli` execution seat, session `019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`, round R33. Executing the branch the
maintainer's ruling on this card already prescribes (comment `5386676209`, 2026-08-23, verbatim):

> **Ruled: settle on the reading, then act** — posture is established WALLED (cli seat's source
> reading), but whether a hosted tenant kernel actually takes the AppPlugin inline-seed branch per
> boot is still one log line / one assertion away. … if the branch IS taken ⇒ implement the
> seed-ledger short-circuit (cloud#1561 shape …); **if NOT taken ⇒ close as single-tenant `os dev`
> cost with the reading attached.** Premise-first: stopping after Step 1 with a negative reading is a
> complete, valid delivery.

The assertion the ruling asks for **already exists**, and it is behavioural rather than a log-string
match. No new code was needed; what was missing was somebody joining the two halves.

### The three links, each measured rather than inferred

**1. Hosted tenant kernel is walled** — established by the source reading in comment `5385089308` and
accepted in the ruling above: `ArtifactKernelFactory` registers `OrganizationsPlugin`
(`@objectstack/organizations`) before `SecurityPlugin`, and per ADR-0093 D5 **fails closed** rather
than degrading when it cannot load it.

**2. `AppPlugin` judges on the live posture, per call** — `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:1345`:

```ts
const tenancy = ctx.getService?.('tenancy') as { posture?: TenancyPosture } | undefined;
if (tenancy?.posture) return postureEnforcesWall(tenancy.posture);
```

Never cached, and never the demoted `resolveMultiOrgEnabled()` — that was #5262's bug and it is fixed.
`plugin-auth` registers the `tenancy` service in kernel Phase 1, before `AppPlugin`'s Phase 2
`start()`, so the service is present on any real boot.

**3. A walled posture provably skips the inline seed** —
`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.tenancy-posture.test.ts` pins the *consequence*, not just the
predicate, with `ql.insert` as the witness (`inlineSeeded: insert.mock.calls.length > 0`) and the
`tenancy` service mocked in the exact `{ posture }` shape `createTenancyService` registers:

| pin | what it establishes |
|---|---|
| `posture-only deployment with a wall in force skips the inline seed` | walled ⇒ **no** `ql.insert` |
| `` `group` is a walled posture too — not just `isolated` `` | both walled postures, not one |
| `single-org deployments still seed inline` | the positive control — the witness can fire |
| `DEGRADED boot seeds INLINE` | the effective-posture case, see the residual below |

Recorded green 20/20 at `38cf397ea9`. I did not re-run it, and I am not citing a stale number as a
fresh one: instead I measured that **neither the subject nor the pin has moved since** —
`git log 38cf397ea9..origin/main` is empty for both `app-plugin.ts` and
`app-plugin.tenancy-posture.test.ts`, at `origin/main` `502ff8b5`. `Test Core` runs
`@objectstack/runtime` on every PR, so that green has been re-earned continuously on unchanged code.

### So the measured cost belongs to the population it was measured on

The rig that produced the 3.02 round trips per seed record is
`scripts/dev-local/bootstrap-curve.mjs` — **dev-local**. The card says so itself: *"In the rig's
kernel the gate reads false and the inline seed runs."* That is now explained rather than left open:
the rig is unwalled, so it takes the inline branch; a hosted tenant kernel is walled, so it takes
`seedSource.suppress('multi-tenant-replay')` and pays the per-org replay path instead — which is
where cloud#1561 already did its work.

The cost is real. It is a **single-tenant / `os dev`** cost, and no hosted environment pays it.

### ⚠️ The one residual, named rather than buried

`DEGRADED boot seeds INLINE` is pinned too, and it is pinned that way on purpose (reading the
*effective* posture is what keeps a degraded stack from booting with no seed data at all). So a
hosted environment launched with `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY=1` **would** pay this cost. Cloud's
factory fails closed rather than degrading, which is why this is a residual and not a hole — but it
is the fact that would reopen this card, and it is a cloud-side reading, not an objectstack one.

Closing `not_planned` per the ruling, with the reading attached. Reopening is free: if a hosted
environment is ever found booting degraded, this card is the record of what it then costs.

⛔ Step 2 (the seed-ledger short-circuit) is not implemented and is not owed — the ruling conditions
it on a positive reading, and the reading is negative.
